To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Tc3A protein-DNA recognition is based on shape-recognition of a bent DNA and that the two TcA domains bind to a DNA oligomer, with the linker between the two domains interacting with the minor groove.

Tc3 transposable element transposition is initiated by the binding of the Tc3A protein to the ends of the transposon DNA and that the protein is able to recognize the transposon ends in a sequence-specific manner.

the DNA-binding domain of a bacterial transposase, the bipartite domain of Tc 3 transposase (Tc3A), has been crystallized in complex to its transposon DNA and that the structure reveals how the protein binds to its target DNA and the DNA is distorted to form a specific complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of DNA recombination.
the structure and function of the transposon Tc3 and the Tc3A-DNA complex.
the molecular mechanisms of transposition, a major mechanism for genetic variation in bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the Tc3 synaptic complex has not been solved, but it can be assumed that a dimeric complex will be formed.
the Tc3A-DNA complex structure reveals how a bipartite DNA binding domain binds to DNA.
the Tc3A-DNA complex represents a new structural class of DNA-binding proteins, which has not been observed before.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tc3A is a novel type of HTH-domain with a unique DNA binding mechanism, which is likely to be relevant for other members of the Tc3 superfamily of transposases.
the structure of the Tc3 synaptic complex is a combination of two different types of DNA binding, one of the type found in the Tn5 transposase and one of the type seen in Pax6.
Tc3A binds to the Tc3 transposition end by two structurally related HTH-domains that are oriented differently from those of the Tn5 transposase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two DNA-binding sites of the Tc3 transposition complex are brought together by the linker, which interacts closely with the DNA, and that this is facilitated by the dimer interface.
the two DNA-binding sites are located on the two ends of the transposon, separated by 40 bp of DNA.
the two DNA-binding motifs in Tc3A are structurally related, but the relative position between them differs from the Pax6 DNA-binding motif.
